guideQuests.ab1.more: Think of a very well-read improv partner. It doesn't check a book mid-scene; it keeps the scene going from what it already knows and what you just said.
guideQuests.ab1.note: An AI model is a program that has read a huge amount of text and writes by guessing what comes next, one small piece at a time. It doesn't look things up while it writes: it only knows what it read before, plus what Marinara sends it with your message.
guideQuests.ab1.title: What is an AI model?
guideQuests.ab10.more: A cook with the spice jar: low temperature sticks to the recipe, high tries something new every time, not always something good.
guideQuests.ab10.note: Temperature is how adventurous the model is. Low plays it safe and can repeat itself; high surprises you and sometimes goes off the rails. Most people never need the other dials; the defaults are fine.
guideQuests.ab10.title: Temperature and other dials
guideQuests.ab11.more: Hiring your actor. You can do it now, or later from Library, Connections.
guideQuests.ab11.note: Pick a service, paste its key, and test it. No account? The Built-in model runs on your computer for free. Not ready yet? That's fine: choose Not now, and everything else still works except chatting.
guideQuests.ab11.title: Set up a model (optional)
guideQuests.ab12.more: A tutor who has read the whole manual and doesn't mind silly questions.
guideQuests.ab12.note: Professor Mari has read every guide in this app. Ask her anything in plain words, or have her build characters and lorebooks with you. She talks through your model, so she needs a working connection to answer.
guideQuests.ab12.title: Meet Professor Mari
guideQuests.ab2.more: Marinara is the stage, the model is the actor. A service rents you an actor over the internet; the Built-in model is an actor who lives in your house: always free, a bit less polished.
guideQuests.ab2.note: Marinara is the app you chat in; the model runs somewhere else. A service on the internet (OpenRouter, NanoGPT, OpenAI and others) runs big models for you with an API key. The Built-in model runs a small one on your own computer with no key.
guideQuests.ab2.title: Where the model lives
guideQuests.ab3.more: The context window is the actor's desk. Only what fits on the desk gets read before each line, and when it's full, the oldest pages slide off the back.
guideQuests.ab3.note: Models read in tokens, small pieces of words (about three quarters of a word each). They can only read so many at once: that's the context window. Every reply, Marinara fills it with the rules, the character, your persona and as much of the chat as fits. Services charge by tokens.
guideQuests.ab3.title: Tokens and context
guideQuests.ab4.more: Summaries are sticky notes on the desk. Memory Recall is a librarian who fetches the one old page you need for this scene.
guideQuests.ab4.note: In a long chat the oldest messages no longer fit, so the model can't see them. Summaries keep a short version of what happened; Memory Recall finds the old messages that matter right now and puts them back.
guideQuests.ab4.title: Why your character forgets
guideQuests.ab5.more: A kitchen has more than one cook. The head chef writes the story; helpers chop, plate and check the oven. In a small kitchen, one cook does everything.
guideQuests.ab5.note: Marinara can give different jobs to different models: Main writes replies, others run helpers, make pictures or answer small questions. One chat model can do all the text jobs to start; add others when a feature asks.
guideQuests.ab5.title: Several models, several jobs
guideQuests.ab6.more: A referee who only says yes or no. Small and fast, so it can check every single reply without slowing the game down.
guideQuests.ab6.note: A Decision model only answers small yes-or-no questions, like "did the scene move to a new place?". Its answers are never shown in the chat; they switch features on and off. It's optional, and the Built-in model can do it for free.
guideQuests.ab6.title: Decision models
guideQuests.ab7.more: A map of meaning: "tavern", "inn" and "pub" land next to each other, so Marinara can look nearby instead of needing the exact word.
guideQuests.ab7.note: An embedding model turns text into a list of numbers that stands for its meaning. Marinara uses it to find lore and memories by meaning, so "blade" can find an entry about a "sword". It never writes anything.
guideQuests.ab7.title: Embeddings
guideQuests.ab8.more: One friend can describe a painting to you; another can paint one. Different skills, often different people.
guideQuests.ab8.note: Some models can look at a picture and describe it (Image reading). Making new pictures is a separate kind of service (Image generation). A chat model that can read pictures still can't paint one.
guideQuests.ab8.title: Reading pictures vs making them
guideQuests.ab9.more: A preset is the stage manager's running order: who's introduced first, which notes go where, and when the actor gets their cue.
guideQuests.ab9.note: Every reply, Marinara hands the model a script: the rules, the character sheet, the story so far, then "your line". That script is the prompt, and a preset decides what goes in it and in what order. Peek prompt in a chat shows the real one.
guideQuests.ab9.title: Prompts and presets
guideQuests.basicsIntro: New to AI? Twelve short stops through the guides: what a model is, the kinds Marinara uses, tokens and context, and setting one up (optional). Each opens the guide at the passage that matters, with a plain-words note. It ends with Professor Mari.
guideQuests.card.mariNeedsConnection: She needs a working connection before she can answer.
guideQuests.da1.more: Save one parameter as a connection default.
guideQuests.da1.note: Account defaults apply everywhere; a chat's own values win for that chat. Temperature and Top P both change randomness, so change one. Max output tokens is a ceiling, not the reply length.
guideQuests.da1.title: Generation parameters: per account or per chat
guideQuests.da2.more: Turn on tool use in one chat and give it one tool.
guideQuests.da2.note: Tools let a model look things up or act during a reply. More tools means more instructions, and some models get confused, so turn on only the ones a chat needs.
guideQuests.da2.title: Function calling
guideQuests.da3.more: Translate one message in a chat.
guideQuests.da3.note: Translate only what you read, or also what you send, and choose which service does it.
guideQuests.da3.title: Translation
guideQuests.da4.more: Give the Agents job a cheaper model than Main.
guideQuests.da4.note: Helper jobs (agents, summaries, decisions) are often fine on a cheaper model; Main needs your best. An If it fails model takes over when one breaks.
guideQuests.da4.title: Models for each job
guideQuests.da5.more: Look at a decision's score in Peek prompt's Decision diagnostics.
guideQuests.da5.note: A higher threshold means fewer false yeses but more missed ones. Time limits keep a slow model from holding up the reply. Plan for wrong answers.
guideQuests.da5.title: Decision thresholds and time limits
guideQuests.dc1.more: Open a Conversation's sticker tab, then the gear, and switch to Tool-call for a few replies.
guideQuests.dc1.note: Semantic (default) ranks them by meaning with a small model on your computer, for free. Tool-call has your chosen model pick, smarter but a call each reply. Random is cheapest and least fitting. Descriptions help: used for ranking they cost nothing; shown to the model they add tokens but teach it that :fine: is sarcastic; sending the pictures needs a vision model.
guideQuests.dc1.title: How characters pick stickers and emojis
guideQuests.dc2.more: Turn on autonomous messages in a Conversation and give the character a schedule.
guideQuests.dc2.note: Characters can text first. The check-in limit sets how often; the schedule decides when they're busy, asleep or free, which is why a character stays quiet at night.
guideQuests.dc2.title: Autonomous messages and schedules
guideQuests.dc3.more: Turn it on in a group Conversation and say something that invites a debate.
guideQuests.dc3.note: Characters reply to each other, not only to you. Livelier group chats, more tokens per turn.
guideQuests.dc3.title: Character exchanges in group conversations
guideQuests.dc4.more: Open a Conversation's summaries and read yesterday's.
guideQuests.dc4.note: Conversations summarize each day. You choose when a day ends and can fill in missing days. A short daily summary keeps months of texting in memory for a fraction of the tokens.
guideQuests.dc4.title: Daily summaries
guideQuests.dc5.more: Link a Conversation to a Roleplay and tell the character something to remember there.
guideQuests.dc5.note: A character remembers its other Conversations (on by default). Linked to a story chat, it can send a one-time influence tag, a lasting note tag (listed under Conversation Notes), and the story character can step out with an ooc tag.
guideQuests.dc5.title: Cross-chat awareness and linked-chat tags
guideQuests.dc6.more: Write a chat-specific About Me for one of your characters.
guideQuests.dc6.note: Give a character a different About Me in one chat. With the update_about_me tool, a character can change its own bio: publicly (you approve first) or only privately.
guideQuests.dc6.title: A different bio per chat, and characters editing their own
guideQuests.dc7.more: Open Schedules and try Vary on one character.
guideQuests.dc7.note: Have the model redraft a character's week: Rewrite (fresh), Adjust (keep most, apply your note), Vary (clearly different but believable) or Repair (fix gaps).
guideQuests.dc7.title: Schedule AI
guideQuests.dc8.more: Upload a sound to the soundboard, or generate an Idle clip for a character.
guideQuests.dc8.note: Characters can play sounds in a call, including your own uploads. Character video presence swaps the still avatar for looping clips: idle, talking, laughing and more.
guideQuests.dc8.title: Calls: soundboard and video presence
guideQuests.dc9.more: Check which games your characters may start in a Conversation's Commands.
guideQuests.dc9.note: Each table game has its own switch under Commands. With one on, a character may start UNO, chess or poker by itself; the slash command works either way.
guideQuests.dc9.title: Characters starting games
guideQuests.de1.more: Make a tool with a static result.
guideQuests.de1.note: Give characters a tool that returns a fixed result, calls a webhook, or runs a script.
guideQuests.de1.title: Custom tools
guideQuests.de2.more: Ask Professor Mari for a tiny extension.
guideQuests.de2.note: Small add-ons of your own, with revisions and recovery if one breaks.
guideQuests.de2.title: Personal extensions
guideQuests.de3.more: Read which entities the integration adds.
guideQuests.de3.note: Characters can trigger smart-home actions, and your automations can send a message or start a reply. A chat can also mirror to Discord, and the Haptic Feedback agent drives a device.
guideQuests.de3.title: Home Assistant automations
guideQuests.deepIntro: For when you know the basics: settings where the choice isn't obvious, and features almost nobody finds. Nothing here is needed for anything else. They join Things to try on Home once you finish its Core trail, favouring what you use most.
guideQuests.dg1.more: Start a game and read the Story style step closely.
guideQuests.dg1.note: What each setup field changes in how the game master tells the story, and how to change them mid-game.
guideQuests.dg1.title: Story style, rating and boundaries
guideQuests.dg2.more: Make a skill check in a game and read how it was decided.
guideQuests.dg2.note: When a skill check rolls dice and when the story decides, and how a ruleset's checks show up.
guideQuests.dg2.title: Dice or story?
guideQuests.dg3.more: Check a campaign's memory after a session ends.
guideQuests.dg3.note: How Advanced Memory carries scenes across sessions, so a long campaign remembers its past.
guideQuests.dg3.title: Game memory
guideQuests.dg4.more: Queue a d20 before your next check.
guideQuests.dg4.note: Queue a d20 from the dice menu, and the next check uses your number instead of a new roll. Modifiers still apply.
guideQuests.dg4.title: Pre-roll your own d20
guideQuests.dg5.more: Win a QTE, or turn them off for your next game.
guideQuests.dg5.note: Timed choices for dodges and chases: faster earns a bigger bonus, too slow costs you. Turn them off on the wizard's Features step for screen readers or untimed play.
guideQuests.dg5.title: Quick-Time Events
guideQuests.dg6.more: Find the eye icon in Session History (you don't have to click it).
guideQuests.dg6.note: Show Spoilers reveals the world overview, story arc and plot twists the GM keeps private. It spoils the plot, so it's a last resort when the story feels lost.
guideQuests.dg6.title: The GM's hidden notes
guideQuests.dg7.more: Open Initial Game Setup in a campaign.
guideQuests.dg7.note: Copy or download the exact setup behind a campaign that worked. Keys are never included, but your preferences and boundaries are, so read it before you post it.
guideQuests.dg7.title: Share the setup that made a game
guideQuests.dg8.more: Open a past session in Session History.
guideQuests.dg8.note: Play a past session again, or edit what happened in it.
guideQuests.dg8.title: Replay or edit a past session
guideQuests.dg9.more: Read the first example and imagine one for your campaign.
guideQuests.dg9.note: Story scripts, HUD widgets and creature packs let you build pieces for Game Mode yourself. For people who want to make content, not only play it.
guideQuests.dg9.title: Write your own story scripts
guideQuests.dk1.more: Give a character a coloured name in Creator's Notes and turn on Exclusive.
guideQuests.dk1.note: A style block in a card's Creator's Notes restyles that character's messages: name colour, bubble, font, even the background. It's off until you pick a Card Theming mode in Chat Settings, Characters (Party in Game): Exclusive (each character's CSS touches only their own messages, best for groups) or Chat (reaches the whole chat area, best for one-on-one). @chat-mode rules aim at one mode. Scripts and anything outside the chat are stripped.
guideQuests.dk1.title: Card CSS in Creator's Notes
guideQuests.dk2.more: Add an alternative backstory and use it in one chat.
guideQuests.dk2.note: One card, a different description, backstory or look in chosen chats (a "Young" version, an AU). Better than copying the card, because fixes to the original reach every chat.
guideQuests.dk2.title: Card field alternatives
guideQuests.dk3.more: Add a one-line Post-History Instruction to a character.
guideQuests.dk3.note: Three places to steer one character. System Prompt sits with the character's block. Post-History Instructions land right before the model writes, the strongest spot. A Depth Prompt slips a reminder a few messages back (4 by default): quieter, but hard to forget.
guideQuests.dk3.title: System prompt, post-history or depth prompt
guideQuests.dk4.more: Restore an older version of a character.
guideQuests.dk4.note: Every save is a version you can restore, and card changes from an agent wait for your review. Experimenting with a card stops being risky.
guideQuests.dk4.title: Version history
guideQuests.dk5.more: Give a character a regex script and set the chat to Exclusive.
guideQuests.dk5.note: Find-and-replace scripts that belong to one character. They do nothing until Scoped Regex Scripts in Chat Settings is Exclusive (that character's messages) or Chat (every message). For a speech quirk or custom formatting.
guideQuests.dk5.title: Character-scoped regex
guideQuests.dk6.more: Add a phonetic name to a character with a tricky name.
guideQuests.dk6.note: Spell how a name should sound in Conversation calls. Calls only: Speak and Game narration ignore it.
guideQuests.dk6.title: Phonetic names
guideQuests.dl1.more: Give one entry a Cooldown of 5.
guideQuests.dl1.note: Four timers make lore feel alive. Sticky keeps a revealed secret in for a few messages, Cooldown stops an omen firing every turn, Delay hides a twist until later, Ephemeral fires an intro once. A 25% probability keeps rumours occasional.
guideQuests.dl1.title: Probability and timing
guideQuests.dl2.more: Put two alternative entries in the same Group.
guideQuests.dl2.note: Entries in one Group are alternatives: only one fires per reply (three kinds of weather). The Stable lorebook picks switch keeps the same winner in a chat while the candidates stay the same, instead of re-rolling every reply. Stable for consistency, re-roll for variety.
guideQuests.dl2.title: Groups and stable picks
guideQuests.dl3.more: Make an Outlet entry and place its macro in a preset.
guideQuests.dl3.note: Position Outlet puts an entry only where {{outlet::name}} sits in your preset, instead of the usual spots. For lore that must land in one exact place.
guideQuests.dl3.title: Outlet entries
guideQuests.dl4.more: Turn on Recursive for one lorebook.
guideQuests.dl4.note: Lets one entry's text trigger related entries: a city pulls in its ruler. Off by default, with a per-entry Recursion switch and a Max Depth. It costs budget, so turn it on only for chains you want.
guideQuests.dl4.title: Recursive scanning
guideQuests.dl5.more: Filter a secret entry to the one character who knows it.
guideQuests.dl5.note: Limit an entry to certain characters, tags or generation types, or scan the card's description for its keys. In Individual group replies a character filter keeps a secret out of everyone else's replies; in Merged replies it doesn't.
guideQuests.dl5.title: Context filters
guideQuests.dl6.note: {{include::Rules of the arena}} pastes an entry's text wherever you write it: in other entries, prompts or cards. One copy of house rules to edit. {{include::Book::Entry}} works even from a book that isn't in the chat.
guideQuests.dl6.title: The include macro
guideQuests.dl7.more: Turn it on, chat a bit, then sort a lorebook by use.
guideQuests.dl7.note: A switch that records which entries actually fired, so the lorebook editor can sort and filter by use. It finds dead entries that never trigger.
guideQuests.dl7.title: Activation stats
guideQuests.dl8.more: Test a sentence against one of your lorebooks.
guideQuests.dl8.note: Paste sample text and see which entries would fire, without sending anything. Faster than testing in a chat.
guideQuests.dl8.title: The Keyword test tool
guideQuests.dm1.more: Whisper something to one character in a group Roleplay.
guideQuests.dm1.note: [whisper: character="name" text="…"] reaches only that character and the narrator. Reveal shows it to you without telling anyone else. You can whisper in your own messages too. For secrets, visions and asides.
guideQuests.dm1.title: Whispers
guideQuests.dm2.more: Leave the narrator a private note.
guideQuests.dm2.note: [notes: content="…"] reaches only the narrator. A note on one message stays private, or goes to one chosen character. For steering without the cast hearing.
guideQuests.dm2.title: Private notes
guideQuests.dm3.more: Hide one message from one character.
guideQuests.dm3.note: In a Roleplay group, Hide from AI lets you pick which characters can't see a message (a crossed-eye marker). /hide does ranges.
guideQuests.dm3.title: Hide a message from some characters
guideQuests.dm4.more: Turn on Interruptions and write a long speech.
guideQuests.dm4.note: [interrupt: part="…"] lets a character cut off your last message mid-sentence. Restore original message undoes it.
guideQuests.dm4.title: Interruptions
guideQuests.dm5.more: Ask for a handwritten letter with /html.
guideQuests.dm5.note: [html: prompt="…"] or /html makes an in-world object: a letter, a sign, a terminal. Each is its own model request (up to 3 per reply); the free Documents kinds are instant for plain pages.
guideQuests.dm5.title: HTML artifacts
guideQuests.dm6.more: Press Send with an empty box.
guideQuests.dm6.note: Send with an empty box retries after your last message, or in Roleplay starts a new turn.
guideQuests.dm6.title: Empty Send retries
guideQuests.dm7.more: Open the branch graph of a chat with branches.
guideQuests.dm7.note: See every branch of a chat as a graph, and import a chat file as a new branch of an existing chat.
guideQuests.dm7.title: The branch graph
guideQuests.dm8.more: Turn it on before your next big cleanup.
guideQuests.dm8.note: A switch that keeps deleted messages so you can bring them back.
guideQuests.dm8.title: Recover deleted messages
guideQuests.dm9.more: Export a chat with reasoning included.
guideQuests.dm9.note: Exports leave out thinking and private notes unless you ask for them.
guideQuests.dm9.title: Reasoning and notes in exports
guideQuests.dp1.more: Add a weighted random line to a preset or entry.
guideQuests.dp1.note: {{random::Common event@1::Rare event@0.25}} makes one option four times as likely as the other. For random events that shouldn't be equally likely.
guideQuests.dp1.title: Weighted random
guideQuests.dp10.more: Look at your provider's docs for one extra parameter.
guideQuests.dp10.note: Raw JSON for settings Marinara has no field for, per account or per chat. Service Tier (OpenRouter, NanoGPT) trades price for speed: Flex is cheaper and slower, Priority faster and dearer.
guideQuests.dp10.title: Custom Parameters and Service Tier
guideQuests.dp11.more: Set a limit of 100 in a long chat and compare the cost.
guideQuests.dp11.note: Send only the last N messages: cheaper and faster, but it forgets more. In Roleplay with Advanced Memory Recall it's ignored, and that feature's compression size is the dial instead.
guideQuests.dp11.title: Context message limit
guideQuests.dp2.note: {{setvar}}, {{getvar}}, {{incvar}} and friends store values that survive across turns and restarts, separately in each chat. A day counter, a mood score, a quest flag.
guideQuests.dp2.title: Chat variables
guideQuests.dp3.more: Add a Random Pick variable to a preset.
guideQuests.dp3.note: A preset can ask questions when a chat starts: an on/off Toggle, a Multi-Select, or a Random Pick (one random option per chat, or with Multi-Select, a fresh draw from your pool each reply).
guideQuests.dp3.title: Preset variable kinds
guideQuests.dp4.more: Write one decision block with sticky:2.
guideQuests.dp4.note: {{#if decision:"a fight starts" sticky:3 cooldown:5}} asks the Decision model, keeps a yes for 3 turns, then rests for 5. decision_choice: picks one of several answers. Test decisions in Peek prompt runs them without writing a reply.
guideQuests.dp4.title: Decision blocks with timers
guideQuests.dp5.more: Move a changing block below the chat history.
guideQuests.dp5.note: Put blocks that change often late in the prompt. A change near the top stops the service reusing everything after it, so you lose most cache savings.
guideQuests.dp5.title: Decision blocks and prompt caching
guideQuests.dp6.more: Add a group block to a group chat's preset.
guideQuests.dp6.note: A [ line, some text with {{char}}, and a ] line repeat once per character in a group chat: "each character's attitude" without writing it out for everyone.
guideQuests.dp6.title: Group blocks
guideQuests.dp7.more: Compare a reply with XML and with Markdown.
guideQuests.dp7.note: XML tags (the default), Markdown headings, or nothing around each preset section, plus Send without wrapper for one block. Switch only if a model behaves better without tags.
guideQuests.dp7.title: Wrap format
guideQuests.dp8.more: Try a short prefill like "*" with a model that supports it.
guideQuests.dp8.note: Assistant Prefill puts words in the model's mouth at the start of its reply; Reasoning Prefill does the same for its hidden thinking (only some models). Some services refuse a prompt that ends on the AI's words, and Marinara moves the prefill for them.
guideQuests.dp8.title: Prefills
guideQuests.dp9.more: Find the switch in a chat's parameters.
guideQuests.dp9.note: On by default: old thinking isn't fed back, which saves tokens and stops loops. Turned off, it replays the last few reasoning blocks.
guideQuests.dp9.title: Exclude Past Reasoning
guideQuests.dr1.more: Turn on Memory Recall in a long Roleplay and ask about something from early on.
guideQuests.dr1.note: Chat Summary is sticky notes: cheap, and you control them. Memory Recall finds old messages by meaning and works with the built-in embedding model. Advanced Memory remembers by scene, per character, for very long stories, with more setup.
guideQuests.dr1.title: Which memory feature?
guideQuests.dr10.more: Attach a lorebook to one agent in a chat.
guideQuests.dr10.note: Give one agent its own lorebook in one chat (combat rules only for the combat agent), without adding it to the main reply.
guideQuests.dr10.title: A reference lorebook for one agent
guideQuests.dr2.more: Switch a group chat between Merged and Individual and compare a reply.
guideQuests.dr2.note: Merged writes one combined reply; Individual has each character answer in turn. Automate active characters asks a Decision model who's in the scene instead of you ticking them. Name Prefix History fixes mixed-up speakers.
guideQuests.dr2.title: Group chats: Merged or Individual
guideQuests.dr3.more: Send a picture to a text-only model with captioning on.
guideQuests.dr3.note: Image captioning describes each picture in words so any model can follow it. A vision model sees the picture itself. Captioning costs a call; vision costs image tokens.
guideQuests.dr3.title: Images for a text-only model
guideQuests.dr4.more: Give one entry a Decision statement and watch it in Active Context.
guideQuests.dr4.note: Keywords are exact and free. Vectors match by meaning and need embeddings. A Decision statement ("the party is in the castle") asks your Decision model. Active Context shows which entries made it in and which were skipped for budget.
guideQuests.dr4.title: Lorebook activation: keywords, meaning or a question
guideQuests.dr5.more: Open an agent's settings in a chat and check its phase.
guideQuests.dr5.note: Trackers run after the reply because they read it. Directors run before because they shape it, so they add to the wait. Knowing which is which explains slow replies.
guideQuests.dr5.title: Agents before or after the reply
guideQuests.dr6.more: Pin a background to a place in a Roleplay.
guideQuests.dr6.note: Pinned places reuse your picture whenever the story returns there. Gallery backgrounds are picked from what you have. Painted ones are made new. In the new layout, Decision checks notice a new place or new weather every reply.
guideQuests.dr6.title: Backgrounds that follow the story
guideQuests.dr7.more: Lock one HUD value in a Roleplay with trackers.
guideQuests.dr7.note: Lock a tracker value that keeps drifting, and the next automatic run leaves it alone. The State Editor edits the whole state by hand.
guideQuests.dr7.title: HUD lock mode and the State Editor
guideQuests.dr8.more: Turn on the Echo Chamber agent in a Roleplay.
guideQuests.dr8.note: A live audience reacting to your scene like a stream chat, in its own movable window. It reads whispers too.
guideQuests.dr8.title: Echo Chamber
guideQuests.dr9.more: Turn on Video clips in a Roleplay with Illustrator set up.
guideQuests.dr9.note: With [video: …] a character asks for a short clip of a key moment instead of a still picture, when the moment is about motion. Needs Illustrator with a video connection.
guideQuests.dr9.title: Video clips in replies
guideQuests.dt1.more: Read the example and change one word.
guideQuests.dt1.note: A theme can add an HTML strip to every message, filled with {{char}}, the message number and more. For status boxes CSS alone can't make.
guideQuests.dt1.title: Message templates in a theme
guideQuests.dt2.more: Set Color Scheme to follow the time of day.
guideQuests.dt2.note: The colour scheme can follow the clock, and a theme can style both looks.
guideQuests.dt2.title: Day and night
guideQuests.dt3.more: Read the hooks table and pick one you'd use.
guideQuests.dt3.note: Hooks such as data-chat-id let a theme restyle one chat or one mode only.
guideQuests.dt3.title: Per-chat looks
guideQuests.dv1.more: Turn on emotion indicators and play a line.
guideQuests.dv1.note: Skip hidden tags, code or bracketed notes when speaking, or send [Low, steady voice] directions to the voice. Emotion directions override the bracket skip, so pick one.
guideQuests.dv1.title: Speech filters and emotion directions
guideQuests.dv2.more: Turn it on for your next game.
guideQuests.dv2.note: Game Mode gives characters without a voice their own random voice, so a crowd doesn't all sound alike.
guideQuests.dv2.title: Random NPC voices
guideQuests.dv3.more: Run one prompt through two profiles on the Test bench.
guideQuests.dv3.note: Save an image style once and test it side by side before using it everywhere.
guideQuests.dv3.title: Style profiles and the Test bench
guideQuests.dv4.note: Queue several picture or video requests instead of waiting for each. Prompt overrides let you edit the templates behind them.
guideQuests.dv4.title: Queued media requests
guideQuests.dv5.more: Ask DJ Mari for a playlist.
guideQuests.dv5.note: An AI playlist maker, and a custom music folder for a chat or a character.
guideQuests.dv5.title: DJ Mari and music folders
guideQuests.dv6.note: Noodle activity flows into chats: choose the modes, how many hours back and how many items, capped at 8,192 tokens.
guideQuests.dv6.title: Noodle carryover
guideQuests.dx1.more: Give a custom agent one keyword.
guideQuests.dx1.note: The agent runs only when a keyword appears in the last few messages. Saves tokens on agents that matter only in some scenes.
guideQuests.dx1.title: Activation keywords for custom agents
guideQuests.dx2.more: Add a second prompt option to a custom agent.
guideQuests.dx2.note: One agent, several prompt variants. Each chat picks one from Prompt Mode without editing the agent.
guideQuests.dx2.title: Named prompt options
guideQuests.dx3.more: Add two models to Shuffle and pick Shuffle in a chat.
guideQuests.dx3.note: A pool of models, one picked at random per reply, plus an If it fails model as a backup (replies show a Fallback label). The Retry failed provider calls switch retries short outages when there's no fallback.
guideQuests.dx3.title: Shuffle and fallbacks
guideQuests.dx4.more: Turn on extended caching if you use a Claude subscription.
guideQuests.dx4.note: Extended token caching keeps the prompt cached for an hour, through long pauses between messages. Fast mode should stay off.
guideQuests.dx4.title: Claude subscription caching
guideQuests.offer.intro: Want a 10-minute tour of the basics? I'll explain what an AI model is, why Marinara uses a few different kinds, and help you set one up if you like.
guideQuests.offer.later: You can skip it and start it any time from Home: Things to try, See all, AI basics.
guideQuests.offer.title: New to AI chat?
